verdict.rationale: Stagehand's own act() primitive drives the page from natural-language element descriptions such as "click the login button", with no selectors needed. observe() discovers actionable elements before acting, and selfHeal re-infers an action when its recorded selector breaks. iframe and shadow DOM traversal are handled automatically, and a community user confirms the generated code is self-healing and resilient to DOM changes. Missing for 10: independent hands-on evidence that actions survive major layout redesigns (the community report covers only minor DOM changes), and no documented limits on self-heal reliability.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drive the page through DOM-understanding action primitives (act/click/type on described elements) that survive selector and layout changes

citations.quote: Write automation in plain English. No selectors or complex syntax.
Turn on `selfHeal` to re-infer an action when its recorded selector breaks.
Control browsers using plain English commands like "click the login button" or "fill out the contact form"
Stagehand automatically handles iFrame traversal and shadow DOM elements without requiring additional configuration.
With Stagehand, the code is self-healing since it's dynamically generating Playwright every time, making it much more resilient to minor DOM changes
